text: Strengthening the RMB while China is still an export-oriented economy brings more flaws than benefits. Even though a lot of China’s raw materials for domestic use are produced locally, lotof the imported inputs are mainly for export production. So if the RMB rises to boost purchasing power, the impact on domestic consumption will be minimal and short-term, while it increases deflation risk and hits the export sector seriously—especially for price-sensitive consumers overseas. China needs other engines to lift domestic consumption or drive global demand, not just a stronger currency.
